executivePulse.interpretation: The situation in memory and AI infrastructure remains strained. Enterprise SSDs, server DRAM / RDIMM and HBM are currently among the most constrained areas. The Daily Check from 2026-08-17 reviewed eight relevant reports; it does not indicate a confirmed material directional change at present. New capacities and improved yields can ease pressure, but will reach the market with a time lag. For buyers, securing supply, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain decisive.

signals.title: Liquid Cooling Becomes Standard for High-End AI Infrastructure, with Penetration Expected to Reach 53% in 2026, Says TrendForce
signals.summary: Liquid cooling penetration among AI chips is projected to rise to 53% in 2026 and approach 60% in 2027. High-end chips from NVIDIA, AMD, and Google are driving the adoption of liquid cooling. NVIDIA’s rack-scale solution shipments are expected to double in 2026, while more than 80% of Google’s AI servers already use liquid cooling.
signals.analysis: This report is relevant for data-centre storage: it can affect prices, available capacities or procurement strategy for enterprise SSDs.

signals.title: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von Reuters: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
signals.analysis: The report alters the build-out trajectory of AI and data-centre infrastructure. Greater productive compute capacity draws server memory, enterprise storage, networking and power infrastructure with it.
